audit_findings.title: Projected growth may omit required funding of earning assets
audit_findings.magnitude: $236.2 million of net pawn-loan and finance-receivable funding in 2025, equal to 70.8% of the $333.5 million anchor; $162.5 million in the first half of 2026, equal to 48.7% of the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth is applied to OE without deducting the incremental pawn loans, inventories, leased merchandise and finance receivables required to produce that growth.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, cash flows related to the funding of new pawn loans, net of cash repayments and recovery of principal through the sale of inventories acquired from forfeiture of pawn collateral and changes in net finance receivables, are included in investing activities.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated methodological mismatch, not merely a general risk: the supplied OE calculation excludes investing cash flows used to fund earning assets, while the valuation capitalizes 6%-9% growth. The omitted funding is large relative to anchor OE. It is not necessarily a dollar-for-dollar OE deduction because principal is subsequently recovered, but a normalized incremental investment requirement could materially reduce forecast cash available to equity.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct annual OE including net funding of all earning assets, separate maintenance funding from growth funding, and rerun every scenario with funding tied explicitly to the assumed growth rate.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition-driven historical growth may be credited without its acquisition cost
audit_findings.magnitude: $475.1 million of acquisition cash outflows in 2025, equal to 142.5% of the $333.5 million anchor, and $76.0 million in 2024
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings raise the historical OE trend and projected growth rate, while the purchase consideration producing those earnings is excluded from OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has historically grown in large part through strategic acquisitions, and the Company’s strategy is to continue to pursue attractive acquisition opportunities if and when they become available.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated: acquisitions are a stated major historical growth source, their post-closing earnings enter the OE history, and acquisition outlays do not. The 2025 cash acquisition spend exceeded the entire anchor, so extrapolating the blended historical trend as costless organic growth is reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Decompose historical OE growth into same-store, de novo and acquired components; then rerun using an organic growth rate or deduct a normalized acquisition investment sufficient to support any acquired-growth assumption.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may not contain the full current-debt interest burden
audit_findings.magnitude: Trailing-twelve-month interest expense of $137.715 million versus $121.293 million in FY2025, a $16.422 million difference equal to 4.9% of the $333.5 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: An equity-level OE numerator retains interest expense, so using a historical anchor with less interest than the current capital structure overstates recurring OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest expense increased 15% to $121.3 million during 2025 compared to $105.2 million for 2024, primarily due to increased outstanding long-term debt balances associated with 2025 acquisition activity.
audit_findings.explanation: The temporal mismatch is demonstrated, but the filed scale is not capable of reversing the valuation conclusion. Even treating the entire $16.422 million pre-tax difference as an OE reduction with no tax shield and applying the bull operating-value multiple would reduce value by approximately $7.33 per share, leaving the $152.81 bull value near $145.48, still far below the $225.62 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the current annual run-rate interest expense from each June 2026 debt instrument, commitment fees and issuance-cost amortization, and rerun the equity OE numerator; retain the finding as non-material unless the confirmed adjustment materially exceeds the filed TTM difference.

audit_findings.title: Gold forwards can suppress future economics without a current accounting charge
audit_findings.magnitude: $58.98 million gross price differential on the original 60,000 ounces using the filed December 2025 spot price of $4,323 and contract price of $3,340; this is not a realized earnings loss
audit_findings.mechanism: Contracted selling prices affect scrap-gold revenue and OE through September 2027 even though normal-sales accounting records no FY2025 mark-to-market charge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company had contractual commitments to deliver a total of 60,000 gold ounces between January 2026 and September 2027 at a weighted-average price of $3,340 per ounce.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a contractual forward-looking exposure rather than a demonstrated FY2025 accounting error. The latest filing shows 43,500 ounces remaining at $3,920, but the record provides no valuation-date gold-price scenario with which to measure the remaining economic effect. The direction depends on future spot prices: value is overstated if modeled prices exceed the contracts and understated if they fall below them.
audit_findings.action: Schedule contracted ounces and prices by delivery period through September 2027, compare them with each scenario's gold-price assumption, and rerun OE using contracted revenue for those ounces.

audit_findings.title: Credit-loss assumptions could overstate sustainable AFF earnings
audit_findings.mechanism: Understated lifetime-loss provisions would inflate reported AFF earnings and the OE anchor; later charge-offs or reserve increases would reduce OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The determination of the allowance for loan losses on finance receivables was subjective and required management to make significant judgments related to the selection and application of modeled loss rates, the incorporation of observable and forecasted economic conditions, and adjustments to address recent and forecasted business trends.
audit_findings.explanation: The record establishes elevated estimation risk but not a reserve error. At December 2025 the finance-receivable allowance was $106.3 million and the OBS liability was $13.8 million. By June 2026, finance-receivable delinquency was 22.3% versus 20.6% a year earlier, and the six-month provision rate rose to 29.2% from 26.8%. Those indicators support concern, but the supplied record does not show the ultimate lifetime performance of the 2025 and OBS vintages, so materiality cannot yet be established.
audit_findings.action: Back-test the 2025 finance-receivable and OBS vintages through contractual maturity against booked lifetime losses, including charge-offs and recoveries, then normalize anchor OE and rerun if realized loss rates exceed the original provisions.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating cash as excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: Maximum $172.298 million, or $3.94 per share, if none of the bridge cash were excess
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding operating or restricted cash to the equity bridge double-counts capital needed to sustain the OE numerator.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s business requires it to maintain a significant supply of cash, loan collateral and inventories, including gold and other precious metals, in most of its pawn stores and certain storage and processing locations.
audit_findings.explanation: The classification of all cash as excess is unresolved, and $69.1 million was held by foreign subsidiaries for operating and growth needs. Nevertheless, even the conservative maximum adjustment of removing the entire $172.298 million would reduce base value from $130.28 to approximately $126.34 per share and bull value from $152.81 to approximately $148.87, both still far below the $225.62 market price. It therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion on the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Determine store-vault, seasonal, regulatory and foreign-subsidiary minimum cash requirements and rerun the bridge using only demonstrably distributable cash.
